item.title: Mohe drives freezing cold temps to its advantage
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
As temperatures drop in Mohe, Heilongjiang province, test vehicles from major manufacturers make a beeline for the city, allowing automakers to push the cars to their limits on the icy test tracks. Mohe, the northernmost city in China, experiences temperatures as low as -53 C and offers arctic-like test conditions for about seven months of the year, attracting engineers from automotive companies across the country to conduct extreme cold environment tests on new vehicles and components. Every winter, Li Chuang, a cold-weather testing engineer at FAW-Volkswagen Automotive Co Ltd, leads his team to conduct durability tests in Mohe. "The testing period in Mohe can last until April, providing an extended period of extreme cold weather to fully simulate various extreme low-temperature conditions and complete vehicle and component durability validation," he said. "Moreover, the complete infrastructure and detailed local support services also attract us to return every winter." "Mohe's cold region automobile testing base is fully equipped with charging stations and dedicated workshops, and site maintenance is well-managed. From handling test-vehicle permits to responding to daily needs, everything is coordinated well, allowing us to focus entirely on vehicle testing." The unique conditions have been transformed into an industrial advantage, allowing the city to boost economic development. Data from the local government show that during the 2025-26 testing season, Mohe attracted 75 companies, over 1,600 test vehicles and more than 2,400 technical personnel. This directly provided over 200 seasonal local job opportunities and boosted revenue in the catering, accommodation and repair industries by 70 million yuan ($10.5 million). The number of car tests continues to rise, establishing the country's northernmost city as a natural extreme cold laboratory for automotive technology iteration. Li Yumei, manager of Mohe Peninsula Holiday Hotel, said before the rise of the car-testing industry, the hotel mainly relied on revenue from tourist traffic, which was strong during the winter ice and snow season but primarily consisted of short-term visitors. "Now, every testing season, a large number of automotive engineers stay for months," she said. "The stable, long-term guest base complements the ice and snow tourism traffic, providing us with two supporting pillars. The overall revenue has significantly increased compared to the past." The thriving hotel industry is supported by a comprehensive government service system. The local government has established a public welfare institution in coordination with the city's bureau of industry and information technology to advance industrial services support. "We have focused on the cold region testing development track, providing precise full-chain services for companies settling here, and continuously nurturing a fertile ground for industrial development," said Wang Dongling, director of the bureau. The local government has also set up a dedicated WeChat group for automotive companies, implemented a 24-hour response mechanism for car companies' needs, and promoted on-site, immediate processing of test vehicle permits to cut waiting times and operating costs. "During the summer period, we comprehensively surveyed and integrated citywide catering, accommodation and maintenance support resources, compiling and distributing service manuals to provide clear guidance for automotive companies," Wang said. The local government also regularly organizes forums and coordinates with companies to address various issues, such as site scheduling, safety training, road support and approvals, providing a one-stop service for processing, site coordination and logistics support. Meanwhile, Mohe is looking beyond automotive testing to broaden the application scenarios of extreme cold testing. Currently, the city hosts six permanent testing institutions, and during the 2025-26 testing season, it undertook testing for over 150 companies, completing low-temperature performance testing of more than 40,000 products. zhouhuiying@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: NZ faces deadlock with election results
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
New Zealand faces uncertainty over its next government after the release of its general election final results on Friday, with neither the ruling coalition nor the main opposition securing a majority, raising the possibility of a return to the polls. The center-right National Party, led by Prime Minister Christopher Luxon, secured 40 of the 130 seats in Parliament, according to the country's Electoral Commission. The three-party governing coalition also includes ACT New Zealand, which had 13 seats, and the New Zealand First Party, which had 12 seats. The left-leaning opposition Labour Party secured 36 seats and, together with the 17 seats of the Green Party, seven seats of the Opportunity Party and five seats of Te Pati Maori, means the total of 65 seats equals the coalition's number which falls short of the parliamentary majority needed to govern. Coalitions are common under New Zealand's electoral system. The results mean Luxon will have to turn to the Opportunity Party to break through and avoid another election, according to public broadcaster Radio New Zealand. RNZ quoted Luxon as saying that "one of the strongest messages" he heard throughout this campaign is that voters "want more cross-party collaboration". "They want their leaders to find common ground and to get on with delivering for them," he said. "I've heard the message, and I'll be taking that into these negotiations," Luxon said, adding that they would be challenging and take time. The results can still be challenged with recounts, with a single seat change set to affect the governing outcome, according to the broadcaster. The existing government will remain in caretaker mode until the next administration is sworn in, with Parliament required to meet by Jan 14, it said. Opportunity Party leader Qiulae Wong said after the release of the final results that her party would seek to form a stable government but did not rule out another election, saying negotiations with other parties are still needed. Pledging kinder, gentler politics as well as action on climate change, Wong's party became the first in decades to form Parliament without a former cabinet minister as leader. She has vowed to work with whichever party has the largest number of seats. But she has insisted her party's "bottom lines" on climate change action, cost of living and cleaning up politics are nonnegotiable. Speaking outside Parliament following the result, she told journalists she expected "challenging" talks. She preaches "pragmatic politics" as a counter to growing polarization, saying she wants to "bring the heat down a little bit and actually just focus on moving the country forward". New Zealand uses a mixed-member proportional system to elect its Parliament. Voters cast two ballots, one for a political party and another for a candidate in their local electorate. Under the system, governments are typically formed by two or more parties that collectively command a majority in Parliament. Agencies and Xinhua contributed to this story.

item.title: Major storm batters US on holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
WASHINGTON — A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations in the United States on Thursday, as New York's famed Macy's parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from a nor'easter battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country's busiest holiday periods. As families gathered for traditional holiday feasts, nearly a million homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, more than 400 flights were canceled and over 2,000 were delayed, mostly along the East Coast, figures from FlightAware showed. New York's famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organizers said was out of an "abundance of caution". Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was canceled for three years during World War II. While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees falling onto power lines and homes. Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption. Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency on Wednesday over the weather, urged residents to take precautions to stay safe. "Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines," she wrote on X. The National Weather Service warned that the powerful coastal storm would bring strong winds, heavy rainfall and significant coastal flooding to East Coast of the US through Friday. The East Coast disruption came as California also suffered weather woes this week with massive waves battering the coast, prompting evacuations in some areas and soaking San Francisco. A series of Pacific storms is expected to continue to affect the West Coast into next week, bringing rain, mountain snow, strong winds, coastal flooding and high surf. AGENCIES-XINHUA

item.title: Special menu prepared for Pakistani astronaut
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
Following his arrival at China's Tiangong space station with Chinese crewmates for the Shenzhou XXIV mission, Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali is already enjoying a selection of carefully prepared meals specially designed by Chinese space food researchers. To accommodate Ali's dietary preferences and halal requirements, researchers from the Astronaut Center of China developed a customized meal plan in advance to provide "cross-cultural, in-orbit nutritional support", China Central Television reported. Before embarking on the Shenzhou XXIV mission, Ali, the first Pakistani national to reach Earth's orbit, and fellow Pakistani astronaut Khurram Daud had received about seven months of intensive spaceflight training at a Beijing-based center. CCTV reported that the food research team conducted in-depth studies of Pakistani food culture, halal regulations and folk customs, as well as local nutritional standards. Drawing on the existing space food inventory, the researchers selected and modified recipes to create a dedicated food supply of more than 100 varieties for the Pakistani astronauts. They also developed seven Pakistani-style space foods, including beef nihari and lamb korma. Chen Junli, a space food researcher at the center, told CCTV that "on the basis of ensuring that energy and nutrients meet standard requirements, we designed recipes suitable for the Pakistani astronaut's first several meals after entering orbit, when light, easily digestible food is needed, and make adjustments according to personal needs". "Given their preference for spices such as turmeric ... we developed foods like curry chickpeas and butter chicken that fit their local culinary features. The entire production line is fully halal. The foods have gone through repeated taste tests and iterative formula optimization, and received positive feedback from the two Pakistani astronauts during trials," Chen added. During the research and development process, Chen and her colleagues also incorporated dietary suggestions from Ali and Daud, making personalized adjustments to the recipes. "An interesting detail is that in our initial recipe design, we planned to provide locally popular spiced milk tea. But after coming to China, they tried Chinese tea and found Chinese black tea very enjoyable. They also liked Chinese rice very much, so they requested more Chinese rice and tea", which was factored into the recipe design, the researcher recalled. Chen said that following the arrival of the Shenzhou XXIV crew, the six astronauts — the three newcomers and the three members of the Shenzhou XXIII mission — were to share a dinner during the handover period. "With full respect to Pakistani dietary habits, we designed a six-person shared meal, and at other times, astronauts can choose their own dining mode as they wish," she said. "All the dishes for the group meal are favorites of both crews, so they can enjoy the food together." Chen said the Shenzhou XXIV mission marked the first real-world application of the Chinese space food researchers' efforts to develop nutritional plans. "From preliminary investigation, ingredient selection, food development and recipe design to the selection of in-orbit dining modes, we have formed a set of reusable procedures and working paradigms, and we can use them to provide standardized support for future international cooperation aboard the Tiangong space station," Chen told CCTV. Wang Ya'nan, chief editor of Aerospace Knowledge magazine, told China Daily that as international cooperation programs aboard the Chinese space station expand in the coming years, astronauts from more countries are expected to take part in joint missions there. This will pose greater challenges for Chinese space food researchers, but it is also a highly positive development, he said. zhaolei@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: Crucial role of capital market emphasized
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-28
An executive meeting of the State Council, China's Cabinet, underscored on Friday the importance of the capital market to the broader economy and called for a stronger role for State-backed funds in stabilizing it, sending Chinese shares soaring in a tech-led rally. Chaired by Premier Li Qiang, the meeting stressed that the capital market is vital to overall economic development, calling for efforts to strengthen countercyclical adjustments and tackle critical reform tasks at the same time. It was the first time that a statement from a State Council executive meeting had explicitly referred to the "national team", a term for State-backed investors that buy shares during periods of market stress. The meeting said that efforts should be made to give greater play to the "national team" in steadying the market and to optimize the quasi-stabilization fund function of State-owned Central Huijin Investment — an arm of China's sovereign wealth fund and a key member of the group — to provide sufficient liquidity. Analysts said the move has given unusual prominence to the capital market's role in economic development. In a rare move, the meeting statement was released during the midday trading break, highlighting the priority that policymakers have attached to shoring up investor confidence. The market responded with a strong surge. The Shanghai Composite Index soared 3.73 percent to close at 3,606.49 points, while the growth-oriented ChiNext Index jumped 11.61 percent, with both posting the biggest single-day gain since October 2024. More than 400 A-share stocks hit their daily upper limits. Liu Chunsheng, an associate professor of economics at the Central University of Finance and Economics, said the capital market helps companies raise funds for industrial upgrading, while its performance affects household wealth and consumer confidence. By describing the market as vital to the broader economy, the meeting gave it greater prominence than earlier statements that emphasized its role as a pivot within the financial system, Liu said, a shift that suggests the additional policy support under consideration could be more substantial. "Market stabilization is shifting from emergency policy reactions to a standing policy framework," said Tao Chuan, chief economist at Guolian Minsheng Securities, with the pledge of a bigger role for the "national team" giving investors a clearer sense of the support they could expect during bouts of volatility. The meeting also stressed the need to improve market-stabilizing mechanisms, give full play to existing policies, and consider and introduce new measures to promote steady and sound development of the capital market. Efforts should be made to encourage listed companies to pay more dividends and step up share repurchases, improve policies to support and guide medium- and long-term funds into the market, and take resolute action to investigate and deal with practices such as financial fraud and noncompliant share reductions, according to the meeting. China Daily learned from people close to the matter that securities regulators are moving to revise buyback rules to make repurchases easier, expand access to a central bank lending facility for buybacks and share purchases, and encourage listed companies with disclosed plans of buybacks and share purchases to accelerate the implementation process. In its financial stability report released on Friday, the People's Bank of China, the country's central bank, also vowed its support for capital market stability, saying it would make effective use of its two monetary policy tools that support the capital market and roll out investment products and risk management tools tailored to long-term investors. Analysts said that Friday's market uplift may mark a turning point for China's A-share market following months of adjustments, as global investors reassess returns from investments in artificial intelligence, with the correction having made shares of some high-quality companies more attractive. Goldman Sachs expects the CSI 300 Index to gain about 10 percent in 2027, while UBS sees the MSCI China Index rising about 13 percent next year. JPMorgan recommends overweighting Chinese mainland and Hong Kong stocks in Asian portfolios. Meanwhile, earlier this month, Oxford Economics raised its forecast for China's GDP growth in 2027 to 4.6 percent from 4.3 percent. Allianz Global Investors has turned overweight on Chinese equities, said Michael Krautzberger, chief investment officer for public markets at the German asset manager, with holdings spanning AI, robotics, automation and autonomous driving, as well as suppliers of energy and storage components. China's energy infrastructure, scientific talent and vast market provide advantages for innovation, with opportunities increasingly extending to small and medium-sized companies, he said. Howard Davies, a veteran financial regulator and former chairman of the UK Financial Services Authority, said that overseas portfolio investment in China is likely to increase as the country's growing innovation capabilities and opportunities for portfolio diversification draw growing international interest. zhoulanxv@chinadaily.com.cn

item.title: In search of Bruce Lee: Legacy beyond the screen
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
What makes Bruce Lee an icon whose influence still resonates more than five decades after his death? To mark the 86th anniversary of his birth, we revisit his legacy through the eyes of three people inspired by his life and philosophy. Joseph Clarke, an Irish Jeet Kune Do practitioner and young Sinologist who recently relocated to China; American filmmaker and kung fu expert Laurence Brahm; and Wang Zhipeng, chairman of the Beijing Wing Chun Martial Arts Association, share their insights into Lee's martial arts philosophy, his Wing Chun roots and the challenges he faced in Hollywood. From his famous "Be water" philosophy to his belief in breaking free from rigid styles, Lee championed adaptability, self-expression and constant self-discovery. Drawing on both Eastern and Western traditions, he used martial arts to challenge stereotypes and bridge cultures. His legacy lives on, inspiring new generations to think beyond convention and forge their own paths.

item.title: Belt and Road Documentary Forum bridges Xinjiang's perspectives to intl screens
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
A compelling story, interesting characters, and international coproductions that share perspectives, talent, costs and risks offer promising opportunities for documentary filmmaking, said Paul Lewis, special board adviser and international documentary consultant at the World Congress of Science and Factual Producers. Speaking at the inaugural Belt and Road Documentary Forum, held from Nov 11 to 13 in Urumqi, capital of the Xinjiang Uygur autonomous region, Lewis drew on his years of industry experience to encourage more productions showcasing the region and its people, technologies and green initiatives to global audiences. Hosted by Xinjiang Broadcasting and Television Station and the Belt and Road Initiative Documentary Consortium (BriDoc) initiated by the Communication University of China, the forum brought together more than 200 documentary producers and directors, decision-makers from broadcasting and streaming platforms, industry representatives and scholars from 18 countries and regions. It aimed to promote international coproduction, copyright trading and global distribution, while exploring market trends and fostering industry connections. Lewis, from Canada, said documentary filmmaking is expensive, labor-intensive and time-consuming, making it difficult for individual countries or organizations to shoulder the costs alone. "For many years, documentary makers have been going out and finding international partners. Now is the time for Xinjiang to become part of that process." He said Xinjiang's extraordinary landscapes, challenges and human stories offered great content for documentary storytelling. "It's a place where some of the most important questions about our relationship with nature are being confronted and answered every day. And the answers to these questions have the potential to inspire audiences far beyond Xinjiang and even far beyond China," he said, adding that the region's innovative solutions could offer lessons to other places. Lewis also stressed the importance of telling intimate personal stories with universal resonance and historical journeys that remain relevant today.

item.title: The world is watching Shenzhou XXIV
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Pakistan's Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has become the first foreign astronaut aboard China's Tiangong space station, where he will carry out experiments developed by scientists in Pakistan. The joint mission marks a milestone in China-Pakistan space cooperation and reflects China's openness to working with partners around the world on space exploration.

item.title: China develops Mandarin BCI for speech restoration
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
Chinese researchers have enabled a patient with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis to communicate through thought alone, marking the country's first clinical trial of a wireless, invasive Mandarin brain-computer interface. Performed in September at Huashan Hospital Affiliated with Fudan University in Shanghai, the procedure involved implanting two 256-channel, minimally invasive electrode arrays into the brain of a patient surnamed Li. When Li forms words in her mind, the system captures neural signals from speech-related brain regions, decodes them via deep-learning algorithms, and translates them into both on-screen text and synthesized speech. For Li, whose ALS has left her barely able to move her lips, the technology has restored both her voice and her agency. "I have rekindled my hope for life," she communicated through the system, her words rendered in a vocal clone of her own voice. "The surgical trauma was minimal, recovery was quick, and I feel comfortable now." Li's descent into silence began in 2024 with tongue numbness, slurred speech, and arm weakness, culminating in an ALS diagnosis in 2025. As the disease progressed, even her husband could understand only about 20 percent of her attempts to speak. After more than a month of postoperative training, Li achieved encouraging results in spontaneous speech tests with theoretical coverage of the entire Chinese lexicon. During attempted speech, the system decodes more than 95 percent of characters in real time at roughly 80 characters per minute. During imagined speech, accuracy exceeds 90 percent at speeds of around 110 characters per minute — outpacing conventional assistive technologies such as scalp EEG or eye-tracking systems, which typically yield fewer than 40 characters per minute. "This first clinical trial has preliminarily verified the safety and effectiveness of the technology, which holds promise for millions of patients with speech impairments nationwide," said Mao Ying, head of Huashan Hospital. He added that the breakthrough not only offers new communication options for patients with dysarthria, but also charts a path toward a Mandarin-oriented BCI technical framework. The milestone represents a leap in overcoming the linguistic hurdles unique to Mandarin Chinese. Unlike English, which relies primarily on phoneme combinations, Mandarin is a tonal language. The syllable "ma", for instance, means "mother", "hemp", "horse" or "scold" depending entirely on pitch inflection. "In the past, international research on speech BCIs mainly focused on English," said Lu Junfeng, associate dean of Fudan University's Institute of Modern Languages and Linguistics and an associate chief physician at Huashan Hospital. "Because Mandarin has a unique tonal system and a vast number of homophones, we could not simply replicate foreign technical routes." To solve this, a multidisciplinary team from Fudan University, the Chinese Academy of Sciences, ShanghaiTech University, and Shanghai-based neurotech firm StairMed engineered a novel dual-target strategy. Using StairMed's wireless BCI system, surgeons implanted ultraflexible electrodes into two distinct brain regions, collecting 256 channels of neural data from each. One pathway isolates phoneme-related articulatory motor signals, while the other captures the tonal neural patterns essential to Mandarin comprehension. "Helping patients speak from their brains is not just about improving quality of life, but about restoring their right to equal expression, allowing them to be seen by the world and embraced by society, even while living with illness," said Lu. Zhang Menghan, dean of Fudan University's Institute of Modern Languages and Linguistics, noted that combining insights from clinical medicine and linguistics not only advances Chinese-language BCIs, but also opens new avenues for understanding the fundamental neural mechanisms of speech perception and production. The implications extend well beyond China. "Of the more than 7,000 languages spoken globally today, over half are tonal," said Li Yuanning, a researcher at ShanghaiTech University. "The technical route we have pioneered can also serve as an important reference for research into other tonal languages." Looking ahead, the team plans to refine decoding accuracy, enhance device portability, and expand clinical trials, with the goal of bringing the technology to more patients with speech impairments nationwide within the next two to three years. "Enabling patients to connect with the outside world through their own forms of expression is the ultimate goal of restoring language function," said Poo Mu-ming, a CAS academician and academic director of the Center for Excellence in Brain Science and Intelligence Technology. "In the future, this could pave the way for true human-machine integration."

item.title: Pakistani minister: China's space mission shows its inclusive approach
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-27
The successful launch of Shenzhou XXIV crewed spacecraft has captured global attention. Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has become the first foreign astronaut to visit China's space station. In an interview with China Daily, Pakistan's Minister for Planning, Development and Special Initiatives Ahsan Iqbal said the mission demonstrates China's inclusive approach to development. By sharing advanced technologies, China can help improve people's lives across the Global South while paving the way for future international partnerships in space exploration. Watch the video!
